S01.question: Nick jokes that Eric will make everyone count their socks. How should Alice respond?

options.label: Play along
options.text: “Then he can start by counting to four,” Alice said. Nick laughed and showed her where the car was waiting.

options.label: Ask where the others are
options.text: “Where are the others?” Alice asked. Nick nodded at the glass doors, where the next member of the group was already waiting.

S01.question: Damir has joined the group without warning. What should Alice do?

options.label: Say plainly that she is surprised
options.text: “I didn't expect you here,” she said. Damir nodded; his face showed that he had not prepared an opening speech either.

options.label: Put the personal conversation off
options.text: Alice looked at the coffee by the window and decided that a two-year-old relationship did not have to be discussed at an airport. First, they had to leave.

S02.question: Damir reads a message about an upcoming meeting. How should Alice respond?

options.label: Ask whether it affects the route
options.text: “Will we have to change the route?” Alice asked. Damir showed her only the meeting date and put his phone away.

options.label: Leave him undisturbed
options.text: Alice turned to the window. She was not going to guess from someone else's screen which plans had already been made for her.

S02.question: Alice tells the group what article she wants to write. How should she continue?

options.label: Ask what the others think
options.text: She looked at her three fellow travellers in turn. It was not easy to answer first; Nick unexpectedly stopped joking.

options.label: Leave the statement without explanation
options.text: Alice did not justify her thought. A silence settled over the car, and it held more than the magazine's plans.

S65.question: Alice unexpectedly asks Damir about his new scar. What should she do now?

options.label: Do not hide the question behind a joke
options.text: She held his gaze. If Damir wanted to answer, she would listen without making his story part of her own.

options.label: Tell him he does not have to answer
options.text: “You don't have to tell me,” Alice added. She did not want to turn someone else's life into an answer to her own unease.

S65.question: After talking with Eric, Alice wants to know more about him. What should she choose?

options.label: Ask when there is another chance
options.text: She remembered the question but did not demand an answer at once: they still had a shared dinner ahead of them.

options.label: Leave it unsaid
options.text: Alice smiled at Eric. The conversation had already been personal enough for the first evening, and she did not want to close every pause.

S03.question: Damir sits by the window, leaving space between them. How should Alice begin?

options.label: Ask what he expects from the trip
options.text: “You didn't come only because of the hospital, did you?” she asked. Damir looked at her more closely before answering.

options.label: Set the work boundaries first
options.text: “I need to finish my article,” Alice said. Damir moved away from the notebook and assured her that he would not get in the way.

S03.question: By the water, Damir prepares to explain an old decision. How should Alice respond?

options.label: Let him finish
options.text: She did not guess his answer in advance. That did not mean agreement, but it left room for the truth.

options.label: Ask him to speak without excuses
options.text: “I need to hear what you decided, not why it was inevitable,” she said. Damir nodded and began again.

S04.question: They are walking by the water, and Nick joins them. How should Alice continue?

options.label: Ask Nick to show what he noticed
options.text: Nick pointed to a barely visible path in the grass. Alice did not take out her camera; she wanted to hear his explanation first.

options.label: Slow down and look at the valley herself
options.text: Alice paused by the railing. Nick matched her pace without urging her to move faster.

S04.question: The conversation reminds Alice of how she and Damir used to be silent. What will she decide?

options.label: Stop treating silence as agreement
options.text: Alice formed the question she had never asked back then. Next time, she wanted to say it aloud.

options.label: Do not judge the present by an old mistake
options.text: She realised that she did not yet know the people they had become well enough. Today it mattered more to look and ask than to pass sentence.

S05.question: The weather changes the plans, and Eric jokes again that he was right. What should Alice do?

options.label: Suggest a useful alternative shot
options.text: She looked at the wet jackets and the car door. Perhaps the story they were looking for was right there.

options.label: Check that everyone is comfortable filming in the rain
options.text: Alice looked around the group. A beautiful image was not worth replacing someone else's discomfort.

S05.question: Nick and Eric argue about the green pastry. How should Alice join in?

options.label: Play along with Nick's joke
options.text: “I think you already have a winner,” she said. Nick ceremoniously lifted the plate.

options.label: Stay out of it and try something else
options.text: Alice chose the cinnamon pastry and listened with pleasure as two grown men argued about icing.

S06.question: Nick calls to them from the lower path. What does Alice feel?

options.label: Want another minute beside Eric
options.text: She held Eric's gaze for another moment before turning. The simple pause felt unexpectedly important.

options.label: Feel calmer knowing the group is nearby
options.text: Alice turned toward Nick's voice. They were not lost, and they were not planning to make the walk a secret.

S06.question: Damir automatically pours her tea without sugar. How will Alice take it?

options.label: Remember how often she hid changes
options.text: She understood that a new habit did not make the old care false. But now she wanted to call things by their names.

options.label: Do not turn tea into a conversation about the past
options.text: Alice smiled and reached for the sugar bowl. Not every small gesture needed to carry a hidden meaning.

S07.question: Nick wonders what he would never film. What should Alice do?

options.label: Give him time to answer
options.text: She did not rescue the pause with another joke. Nick looked at his fork and searched for the words.

options.label: Ask what matters more than a successful shot
options.text: “Where is your boundary?” Alice asked quietly. Nick stopped turning the fork.

S07.question: During the game, Nick tries to sing without words. How should Alice keep the evening going?

options.label: Join his ridiculous rhythm
options.text: Alice tapped the beat with a spoon against her mug. Nick thanked her with a bow, completely missing the note.

options.label: Offer the next game card
options.text: She put a new card on the table. Nick declared that his talent simply had not been appreciated yet.

S08.question: Damir puts away the medical kit. How should Alice respond to his care?

options.label: Thank him without discussing the past
options.text: She noticed how carefully he fastened the kit. Simple help did not have to conceal another request.

options.label: Ask about the scar and his habit of carrying the kit
options.text: “Have you been travelling with that for long?” Alice asked. Damir looked at his wrist and prepared to answer.

S08.question: Nick points the camera at Damir's kit. What should Alice suggest?

options.label: Ask Damir's permission first
options.text: “It's his story,” Alice said. Nick lowered the camera until he had an answer.

options.label: Film the hands and the kit instead of the face
options.text: Alice pointed to the tools. The detail could say something about Damir's work without a close-up he had not chosen.

S66.question: After working in the greenhouse, Alice chooses how to begin her note. What will she do?

options.label: Describe how they fixed the tag mix-up together
options.text: She remembered the trays and the hands stained with soil. The small shared task said more about the group than a general conclusion would.

options.label: Describe the unexpected hour without cameras
options.text: Alice wrote that for an hour nobody tried to perform another life. The details of that hour deserved a paragraph of their own.

S66.question: Talking with Eric, Alice does not want to rush to a conclusion. What will she keep?

options.label: The wish to know him beyond work routes
options.text: She smiled, imagining Eric in an ordinary house where nobody asked him to check the forecast.

options.label: The right not to decide anything about them today
options.text: Alice felt that a good evening did not need an immediate name.

S09.question: At the waterfall, the noise drowns out the conversation. What should Alice do?

options.label: Move away and talk with Eric
options.text: Eric led her to a dry patch. Only there did Alice hear him laugh without trying to compete with the water.

options.label: Stay by the water and show that she understands
options.text: Nick repeated her ridiculous gesture behind the camera. They both laughed without ever explaining the joke.

S09.question: The boy gets his lost mitten back. What should Alice suggest to Nick?

options.label: Keep the return in the film if the family agrees
options.text: Nick asked the parents whether they wanted the moment included. Alice noted that small meetings like this could tell the story of a road better than a waterfall view.

options.label: Do not film the child; record her own observation
options.text: Alice opened her notebook. She did not need someone else’s close-up to keep the way everyone forgot about filming for a minute.

S10.question: Alice notices how Eric changes when he hears a familiar song. What does she think?

options.label: Want to know what else he hides behind his calm
options.text: She remembered his expression. Maybe one day he would tell her on his own where the music came from.

options.label: Share the minute without asking questions
options.text: Alice did not hurry to fill the silence with questions. The song was playing, and for once that was enough.

S10.question: Eric puts aside an old postcard he is not ready to sign. What should Alice do?

options.label: Do not demand an explanation
options.text: She did not ask for the addressee’s name. Everyone carried things they had to return to in their own time.

options.label: Offer help if he wants to talk
options.text: “If you need a second reader, tell me,” Alice said. Eric nodded and put the postcard back.

S11.question: Nick moves toward dangerous water for a reflection. How should Alice respond?

options.label: Ask him to move away immediately
options.text: “Nick, not here,” Alice said. He looked up, and Eric was already walking toward him.

options.label: Call Eric, who knows the safe boundary
options.text: Alice called for Eric. He turned to Nick at once, while the wave was still far away.

S11.question: After the group moves away from the water, what will Alice do with Nick?

options.label: Walk the dry path with him
options.text: Alice walked a short stretch there and back with Nick while he recorded their footsteps instead of another risky shot.

options.label: Listen to the footsteps together
options.text: She took one earbud. They heard the same footsteps on the dry path without deciding in advance what belonged in the film.

S12.question: Damir says that his life continued after the breakup. What does Alice think?

options.label: They each really had two separate years
options.text: She noticed that she still measured his news against her own biography. Now she wanted to hear his story without comparison.

options.label: This is not yet a promise of a new life together
options.text: Alice did not mistake his openness for a ready-made decision. First they needed to understand who they had both become.

S12.question: Damir notices the word “we” in the draft. What does Alice want to emphasize?

options.label: Not filming was her own decision
options.text: She remembered stepping away from the dangerous place herself. Four people had not needed one author for that decision.

options.label: The others accepting it matters too
options.text: Alice looked at Damir. Sometimes a shared “we” meant precisely that they could refuse together.

S13.question: Nick asks what to do if a good piece of material needs someone’s face. What should Alice say?

options.label: Ask the person instead of relying on silence
options.text: Alice suggested a simple order: the person first, the camera second. Nick went quiet and considered what that would change in the film.

options.label: Keep sound or hands if the person does not want to be filmed
options.text: “The story remains even without a face,” Alice said. Nick looked at the recorder in his bag.

S13.question: Marina asks what they will have instead of postcards. How should Alice answer?

options.label: Name one concrete moment from the road
options.text: Alice remembered how they had made room for someone else’s pace. It was already the beginning of a story, not a slogan.

options.label: Ask for time until the next stop
options.text: She decided not to send a beautiful promise before she understood what she could actually show the reader.

S14.question: Eric finally offers Alice the choice of pace. What will she decide?

options.label: Go first while he stays beside her
options.text: Alice chose a short stretch and looked back: Eric was an arm’s length away, not correcting her choice.

options.label: Ask him to walk beside her, not ahead
options.text: “Then beside me,” she said. Eric put away the phone with the map and matched her step.

S14.question: Eric admits he is learning to ask instead of deciding for others. What will Alice say?

options.label: Support him with a simple invitation to continue together
options.text: Alice nodded toward the trail. She liked that neither of them was turning the walk into a test.

options.label: Say that arguing with him feels safe today
options.text: She said it quietly. Eric smiled and, for once, did not answer with useful advice.

S15.question: Nick pauses by the glacier lagoon. What should Alice do?

options.label: Ask why he is not reaching for the camera
options.text: Nick looked at the water and spoke about a film he had once been afraid to show an audience.

options.label: Wait until he decides to tell her
options.text: Alice sat beside him. After a few minutes, Nick spoke not about the shot but about what remains after a screening.

S15.question: After Nick talks about the unfinished film, what will Alice leave in the draft until tomorrow?

options.label: Keep only the boundary she actually saw
options.text: She left room for the line about Nick lowering the camera, but did not explain his fear for him. He should recognize his own words.

options.label: Leave the material open for both of them to review
options.text: Alice closed the file with a blank space for Nick. Until their conversation, she would not turn his personal confession into a finished paragraph.

S16.question: Damir has just helped the injured tourist and asks for ten minutes without questions. How will Alice respect that boundary?

options.label: Stay nearby without pulling him into a talk
options.text: Alice sat in the neighbouring chair and left the small table between them. She did not turn his help into another examination of their past.

options.label: Give him quiet without guessing his answer
options.text: She nodded and let the room stay quiet. Damir could decide whether to join the others later, without her reading his silence as an answer.

S16.question: At the kitchen table, what boundary will Alice keep around tomorrow’s draft?

options.label: Show each person only recognizable lines
options.text: Alice said that each person would see the lines where they could recognize themselves before anything went to Marina. The draft would not speak for them.

options.label: Leave today’s help outside the draft
options.text: She kept the tourist’s injury out of the draft. It happened in front of everyone, but it was not Alice’s material without a separate agreement.

S17.question: After the shared dinner, Alice has some time. What should she do?

options.label: Help clear the table and stay by the map
options.text: Alice stacked plates by the sink. Eric unfolded the map, and for a few more minutes the evening belonged to all four of them.

options.label: Step outside to the car for a few minutes
options.text: She took her jacket and looked at the rain-soaked parking lot. Nick followed with a question about whether she had lost her phone.

S17.question: Before accepting an invitation, Alice asks herself...

options.label: Do I want to stay close to this person?
options.text: She decided to answer an invitation from her own desire, not from fear of hurting someone. The evening became a little simpler.

options.label: Do I need quiet tonight?
options.text: Alice allowed herself not to decide immediately. Even two hours alone could be a real choice, not a refusal of everyone.

S18.question: After the story about childhood, Alice wants to name her own pace more precisely. What will she say?

options.label: That she does not have to hurry beside him
options.text: “I don't have to keep up with someone else's pace,” Alice said. Eric nodded without turning her words into a ready-made explanation.

options.label: That the memory needs no conclusion
options.text: She smiled: sometimes it was enough to remember where she had once feared falling behind, without making it a rule for today.

S18.question: Alice has returned Eric's thermos, and they walk on. How will she answer the closeness?

options.label: Leave the pleasant possibility without a promise
options.text: Alice let the pleasant possibility remain only a possibility. They walked side by side to the guesthouse without assigning a continuation to the moment.

options.label: Return to the conversation about the road
options.text: She pointed to the sign turned by the wind. Instead of guessing about the future, Alice suggested checking the nearest turn.

S19.question: Nick turns the pool game into a competition. What will Alice do?

options.label: Play along with his sporting ambition
options.text: “All right, but no attempts to re-edit the finish!” Alice said. Nick promised to lose only once.

options.label: Suggest simply swimming beside him
options.text: Nick slowed down and stopped counting the lanes. They reached the wall discussing the most ridiculous film titles.

S19.question: Nick asked before acting. What will Alice notice in that?

options.label: The question came before her answer
options.text: She noted not the evening's result but its order: first the question, then her answer. That was enough to see a change without making new promises.

options.label: Not turn the question into proof
options.text: Alice did not turn one question into a conclusion about him or about them. What mattered was that he had left room for her own answer today.

S20.question: The shopping bag tears by the store entrance. How will Alice react?

options.label: Laugh with Damir
options.text: She did not look for someone to blame for the torn handle. Damir gathered the scattered food and smiled back at her.

options.label: Thank him for helping without looking back at the past
options.text: “Good catch,” Alice said. It was ordinary gratitude, not a request to return to who they had been.

S20.question: After they made room for the neighbours in the kitchen, what will Alice notice?

options.label: A conversation need not displace other people's lives
options.text: She noticed that their conversation continued not because the others disappeared, but because there was room for everyone.

options.label: A pause did not break their conversation
options.text: When the neighbours' kettle began to hum, Alice did not force the conversation back to its earlier pace. The pause became part of the evening.

S21.question: Alice edits her letter to Marina. What principle should remain at the heart of the piece?

options.label: Write about concrete shared decisions, not other people's private secrets
options.text: She returned to the paragraph about the group and removed a detail no one had given permission to publish.

options.label: Do not hide her own role in the journey
options.text: Alice kept “I” in the draft wherever she had actually made the decision herself.

S21.question: After sending the letter to Marina, how will Alice spend the rest of the evening?

options.label: Go out briefly to the waterfront
options.text: She put her phone on charge and took her jacket. A night walk did not have to become another assignment for the article.

options.label: Read the letter once more and let it go
options.text: Alice checked that she had not left an unapproved name in it, closed the screen, and went for her jacket.

S61.question: Ragna tells Alice about her work at the small café. What will Alice ask?

options.label: What is a day like when there are few guests?
options.text: Ragna described an ordinary morning and laughed: there was less free time than tourists imagined.

options.label: What does she herself like most about this place?
options.text: She told Alice about the smell of bread before opening. Alice remembered the answer without taking out her interview notebook.

S61.question: After the conversation and buying the cup, what will Alice keep for herself?

options.label: Not justify the purchase to her friends
options.text: Alice adjusted the box in her bag. She did not have to explain why an ordinary cup mattered today.

options.label: Tell the group about meeting Ragna, not about the object
options.text: She decided to mention the coffee conversation if someone asked about the walk. No one required a report on her free day.

S22.question: The weather changes the group's route. What will Alice do?

options.label: Suggest stopping to discuss the plan calmly
options.text: Eric parked by the service station. While everyone looked at the map, Alice wrote down what could not be promised to the reader.

options.label: Ask Eric to suggest a safe option
options.text: He explained two routes and named the time without flattering round numbers. Alice chose to listen rather than argue with the forecast.

S22.question: Alice says what she will write after the route changes. How will she keep her voice?

options.label: Show her own decision, not only the group's agreement
options.text: She singled out the moment when she herself suggested another road. It belonged in the article.

options.label: Do not make herself the hero of other people's stories
options.text: Alice decided she could name her own choice without claiming the decisions of the people travelling beside her.

S23.question: Eric says that the school will affect his ordinary life. What will Alice ask?

options.label: How does he want to combine school and personal time?
options.text: Eric did not promise a ready schedule. Alice asked how he planned to leave room in the future school for ordinary life, not only classes.

options.label: Does he need Alice's participation in the decision now?
options.text: “I need a conversation, not agreement on my behalf,” Eric answered. Alice could listen without feeling she already had to move.

S23.question: Eric offers to show Alice the first version of his text. How will she agree?

options.label: Read one page over breakfast
options.text: She could give useful feedback without becoming the editor of his entire work.

options.label: Clarify which comments he actually wants from her
options.text: Alice asked him to specify where he wanted a reader's view and where he had to make the decision himself.

S24.question: Nick offers to review film fragments featuring Alice. What will she answer?

options.label: Agree to see only the shots with herself
options.text: “Let's start with the parts where I am,” Alice said. The other people's stories required separate conversations with their subjects.

options.label: Remind him to get the other participants' consent first
options.text: Nick nodded and opened only the fragments he could show Alice without exposing someone else's private conversation.

S24.question: Nick has offered two different possibilities. What will Alice clarify before choosing?

options.label: What the viewing would ask of her
options.text: She kept the work invitation separate from the simple wish to stay together. She could consider one without answering the other immediately.

options.label: Whether she can stay beside him without opening the material
options.text: Alice kept both possibilities distinct: she could continue the morning beside Nick or discuss the fragments, without turning one into a promise of the other.

S25.question: Damir has already told her about a possible interview, but there is no decision yet. What will Alice keep in the conversation?

options.label: Separate his work choice from her feelings
options.text: She heard a possible job in his account, not a request to choose for him. One did not cancel out the other.

options.label: Not turn uncertainty into a promise
options.text: Alice left room for the question of distance: they did not yet have to decide for both of them what the interview would bring.

S25.question: Before S25-C1, what clarity does Alice want to keep for herself?

options.label: Separate what is known from what is not decided
options.text: She held on to two facts: the interview was possible, and its result was still unknown. That was enough not to decide everything in one conversation.

options.label: Name the question that needs an honest answer
options.text: She formulated the question of what would change if Damir left, without demanding an answer he did not have yet.

S58.question: Everyone in the shop has taken on part of the shared dinner. What will Alice notice?

options.label: No one has to decide for everyone
options.text: She looked at the purchases and understood: Eric checked the pot, Nick argued about sweets, Damir chose ingredients, and she could choose her own step.

options.label: Different decisions can become one dinner
options.text: She did not compare their ways of helping. One dinner could hold precision, a joke, and the right to choose separately.

S58.question: The owner brings mustard to their dinner. How will Alice accept the help?

options.label: Thank her and offer her a seat for a minute
options.text: The owner smiled and declined: other guests were waiting. But she told them where she had bought the mustard.

options.label: Help her clear the table for the other guests
options.text: Alice moved the pot aside. There was room for everyone in the kitchen, and dinner stopped being only their group's responsibility.

S26.question: Before choosing a direction, Alice understands...

options.label: I need to take the first step myself
options.text: She put away her phone and decided to name her desire first, then hear the other person's answer.

options.label: I have the right not to answer out of politeness
options.text: Alice remembered several invitations during the trip. None of them seemed like an obligation now.

S26.question: What principle does Alice want to keep in the decision she has just made?

options.label: Not turn someone else's desire into her obligation
options.text: She kept a simple principle beside the decision: someone else's hope did not become her obligation. Her answer had to begin with her own choice.

options.label: Leave room for her own pace
options.text: Alice reminded herself that clarity did not require giving up work, friendship, or time alone. The decision had to fit into her life, not replace it.

S27.question: A few free minutes remain by the shore. What will Alice do?

options.label: Ask everyone to wait and take a group picture
options.text: Nick put the camera on a stone and reached the others just in time for the shutter. Nobody had to pose for the frame.

options.label: Keep the moment without a group picture
options.text: Alice remembered Damir holding the car door while Eric argued with Nick about the route. The camera stayed in the bag.

S59.question: They are choosing the next song in the car. What will Alice suggest?

options.label: Play something everyone knows
options.text: Nick started the chorus. Damir unexpectedly knew the second verse, and the song collapsed into shared laughter.

options.label: Listen to something new
options.text: Alice played an unfamiliar melody. At first no one spoke; by the end Eric asked her to send him the title.

S28.question: Eric suggests turning off the planned trail. What will Alice do?

options.label: Agree to an unplanned stop
options.text: They found a bench beside a small pier. Eric put away the map, and Alice realised she was no longer waiting for his next instruction.

options.label: Ask him to show where the trail leads first
options.text: Eric pointed out the turn and let her choose the next step. When they returned to the car, both considered the walk their shared idea.

S49.question: Music is coming through an open door. What will Alice do?

options.label: Invite Eric to dance first
options.text: “Can you dance?” he asked. “We’re about to find out,” Alice said, taking his hand.

options.label: Suggest simply standing together
options.text: They listened to the music by the wall. A minute later Eric took her hand, but did not lead her anywhere against her will.

S29.question: Nick suggests watching a difficult fragment together. What will Alice ask for?

options.label: Keep her uncertainty in the frame
options.text: Nick did not search for a more flattering take. Alice saw herself on the recording for the first time and did not want to look away.

options.label: Show what he felt at the time
options.text: Nick played the recording without sound and told her what he had been afraid of behind the camera. Alice listened without discussing the edit.

S52.question: Nick has found the lost glove. What will Alice do?

options.label: Warm his cold hands with hers
options.text: Nick stopped joking about the discovery. For a second, it seemed to both of them that they did not have to return to the conversation.

options.label: Suggest looking together for the other glove
options.text: They turned the car upside down until Eric pointed to the back pocket of the seat. Nick admitted Alice had won.

S30.question: Damir asks whether they could build a new habit together. What will Alice suggest?

options.label: Speak plainly about what is difficult
options.text: They agreed to stop when a conversation turned into a competition. Damir repeated her words to make sure he had understood.

options.label: Start with one small shared task
options.text: Alice asked him to make breakfast with her the next day. Damir said that this time he would ask before buying the ingredients.

S55.question: The horse named Noise will not approach the fence. What will Alice do?

options.label: Wait without reaching out
options.text: Alice stood by the fence until the horse turned its head on its own. Damir noticed that she had not once tried to hurry him.

options.label: Ask the handler how to meet him
options.text: The handler explained where it was safer to stand. Damir stepped away, leaving Alice room to decide for herself.

S31.question: Alice finds a story that does not belong in her article. What will she do?

options.label: Write it down only for herself
options.text: She closed the notebook halfway through the page. Some details mattered even if they would never become material.

options.label: Ask permission to return to the story later
options.text: The person she had spoken to offered to write after the trip. Alice kept the contact without promising publication.

S62.question: In the bookshop, Alice is choosing what to take home. What will she choose?

options.label: Buy a book for pleasure
options.text: She did not search for a practical justification for the purchase. The book sat heavily in her bag and somehow made the day lighter.

options.label: Choose a postcard of somewhere she wants to return to
options.text: Alice addressed it to herself with today's date. She set no deadline for returning.

S32.question: Eric's plans do not fit Alice's schedule. What will she do?

options.label: Name her own free time without yielding it
options.text: Eric opened the calendar and offered two days that genuinely suited them both. Neither of them had to pretend that work did not exist.

options.label: Ask to talk about expectations first
options.text: They discovered they were not arguing about hours, but about who was always expected to adjust. Planning became easier after that.

S50.question: Eric puts away the map in an unfamiliar city. What will Alice suggest?

options.label: Choose a street at random
options.text: They turned a corner and found a small bakery. Eric admitted he had not known it was there and bought two identical pastries.

options.label: Ask a passer-by for the way to the waterfront
options.text: The answer took longer than the walk. Alice listened to the local accent, while Eric did not try to hurry the conversation for once.

S33.question: Nick shows a teaser in which Alice recognises herself. What will she do?

options.label: Say which moment she does not want shown publicly
options.text: Nick marked the timeline and removed the shot from the shared version. He did not ask for an explanation.

options.label: Ask why he chose that moment
options.text: Nick said he had wanted to show her alive, not flawless. Alice understood the intention, although they had not decided whether the shot should remain.

S53.question: Nick promised a day without the camera. What will Alice suggest?

options.label: Invite him on a walk without a plan
options.text: They left the house without checking the time. For the first time on the trip, Nick did not ask where the light would be best.

options.label: Suggest cooking a simple dinner together
options.text: Nick mixed up the shelves of spices, and Alice did not rescue the dish immediately. The evening turned out tastier than they expected.

S34.question: Damir cancels the evening, and Alice needs to answer. What will she say?

options.label: Say it hurts, but offer to discuss why
options.text: Damir did not make a joke of it. He explained what had happened. Alice did not agree with everything, but she stopped guessing.

options.label: Suggest spending the evening separately
options.text: She went for a walk, while Damir stayed to deal with his own things. In the morning they met without a quarrel that had been allowed to build.

S56.question: What does Alice want to do during the dance with Damir?

options.label: Move a little closer and hold his hand herself
options.text: She shortened the distance without trying to recreate their old dance. Damir adjusted to her movement.

options.label: Stay close, but let the song end without new promises
options.text: She listened to the music and sometimes met his eyes. For the first time, silence did not mean that they were hiding something.

S35.question: Marina asks for an outline that does not reveal anyone else's private words. What will Alice offer?

options.label: Facts and agreed quotes
options.text: Alice listed the fragments she was already allowed to use. There were enough for an honest piece.

options.label: Name separately what will not enter the article
options.text: She set the boundary without referring to anyone else's secrets. Marina received an answer about the work, not new gossip.

S63.question: The concert has already begun. Where would Alice like to listen?

options.label: Move a little closer to the stage
options.text: She changed seats and, for the first time that evening, stopped looking around for familiar faces.

options.label: Stay by the wall and listen from farther away
options.text: From there she could see the violinist and the windows. Alice kept time with the toe of her shoe.

S02: On the road, Alice remembered Nick joking about the socks and, for the first time, felt like part of the group rather than a guest observer.
On the road, she remembered asking Nick about the others right away. It was easier to meet people when she chose the first question herself.
S08: Over breakfast, Nick remembered how Alice had not rushed him when he answered about filming. He spoke on his own about shots better left unfilmed.
Over breakfast, Nick returned to her question about boundaries. He told her which shot he would never film, even for a good movie.
S22: Remembering how they had cleared the dishes and map together after the shared dinner, Alice suggested stopping first to discuss the road.
Remembering their short walk to the car after the shared dinner, Alice did not apologise when she asked for a minute to herself.
S27: After the evening decision, Alice was no longer going to wait for someone else to name her desire for her.
After the evening decision, Alice remembered that politeness did not oblige her to promise closeness.
